title: Platform systems & services: runbooks, dashboards, alerts, retrospectives, and roadmap
author: Elena Kim
content:
Overview

This document captures the canonical platform-engineering playbook for Redwood Inference: our systems and services inventory, standards for dashboards and alerts, runbook templates, retrospective cadence and format, and the near-term roadmap. It is intended as the single source of truth for platform owners, oncall engineers, and partner teams.

Scope

- Applies to all production-facing services owned by eng-platform, eng-infra, and eng-serving-runtime.
- Covers monitoring standards (dashboards + alerts), incident runbooks, post-incident retrospectives, and roadmap commitments that impact SRE/Platform operations.

Ownership and contacts

- Platform Product Owner: Miguel Torres (product)
- Platform Engineering Manager (runbooks & oncall): Elena Kim (engineering) — author/owner of this doc
- Oncall rotation: platform-oncall@redwood.com (primary escalation)
- Pager escalation: see runbook section for service-specific contacts

Systems & services inventory (summary)

For each service we maintain a short record in the team wiki with: owner, criticality, SLOs, dashboard link, runbook link, and deployment pipeline. Below is the canonical inventory summary table (abbreviated):

- runtime-gateway (owner: Eng Serving Runtime) — Critical (P0) — SLO: 99.95% p99 latency < 200ms — dashboard: /dashboards/runtime-gateway — runbook: /runbooks/runtime-gateway
- request-router (owner: Eng Platform) — High (P1) — SLO: 99.9% availability — dashboard: /dashboards/request-router — runbook: /runbooks/request-router
- batch-ingest (owner: Eng Infra) — Medium (P2) — SLO: job success rate 99% — dashboard: /dashboards/batch-ingest — runbook: /runbooks/batch-ingest

Standards: dashboards and alerts

Goals
- Provide clear, actionable dashboards for service health, user impact, and cost signals.
- Prefer SLO-driven alerting: alert on SLI degradation, not on noisy internal metrics.

Dashboard structure (required panels)
- Overview: availability, error budget burn, and p95/p99 latency trends (30d, 7d, 1d).
- Traffic: RPS, active requests, and request size distribution.
- Errors: 5xx by path, client vs server errors, and error-rate by deployment.
- Capacity & infra: GPU utilization, queued requests, autoscaler decisions.
- Cost signals: tokens/sec, estimated $/hour for serving fleet (approx).
- Recent deploys: last 10 deploys with failures or rollbacks flagged.

Alerting policy (SLO-first)
1) SLO-based alerts (primary):
   - Error budget burn rate (90m window) > 5x baseline -> SEV2 Alert to platform-oncall
   - Error budget consumed > 50% in 24h -> SEV1 if growth trending and customer impact present
2) Symptom-based alerts (backup):
   - p99 latency increase > 2x baseline sustained for 5m -> SEV2
   - 5xx rate > 0.5% of traffic sustained for 5m -> SEV2
3) Infrastructure alerts (informational -> paging when coupled with SLO breach):
   - Node GPU memory pressure > 85% for >10m -> informational unless impacting SLOs
   - Autoscaler dropping below min replicas -> SEV2 if capacity loss causes queueing

Alert ownership and routing

- All platform alerts route to platform-oncall Slack channel and the rota. Pager duty escalation follows the standard 15/30/60 minute policy (see runbooks).
- Alert runbooks must include: definition, symptoms, immediate mitigation, longer-term remediation, owner, and rollback criteria.

Runbooks: templates and examples

Runbook template (required fields)
1) Title
2) Service and owners (primary, secondary)
3) Severity definitions (SEV1/SEV2/SEV3)
4) Symptoms observed (what metrics/alerts indicate)
5) Immediate mitigation steps (ordered, testable)
6) Investigation checklist (logs, traces, deploy history, config changes)
7) Mitigation verification steps
8) Post-incident actions and remediation owner
9) Related dashboards/queries and links

Example excerpt: runtime-gateway SEV2 (p99 latency spike)
- Immediate steps:
  1. Check p99 latency panel and error budget burn on runtime-gateway dashboard.
  2. If error budget burn > 3x baseline, enable traffic shed to dedicated low-latency tier: `kubectl scale --replicas=3 deployment/runtime-gateway-lowlatency`.
  3. Roll back last deploy if deploy timestamp correlates with onset (`/ci/deploys`), command: `kubectl rollout undo deployment/runtime-gateway --to-revision=<rev>`.
- Investigation:
  - Collect traces (`jaeger`) for the 5-minute window.
  - Check KV-cache hit ratios in the runtime cache dashboard.

Incident lifecycle and SEV definitions

- SEV1: Production outage or customer-facing degradation affecting > 50% of latency-sensitive traffic — escalate immediately (page primary oncall).
- SEV2: Partial degradation (latency or error-rate increase) affecting a subset of requests — page oncall and notify owners.
- SEV3: Low-impact issues or non-urgent failures — ticket in backlog and monitor.

Retrospectives and blameless postmortems

Cadence and ownership

- All SEV1/SEV2 incidents require a blameless postmortem within 72 hours of incident resolution. The oncall owner is responsible for drafting; the service owner is responsible for publishing.
- Retrospective template includes: timeline, root cause, immediate mitigations, action items (owner + due date), and cross-team implications.

Retro meeting format (30–60 minutes)
1. Objective recap and impact summary (5–10m)
2. Timeline review (10–15m)
3. Root cause and contributing factors (10–15m)
4. Action items and owners (5–10m)
5. Publish and track in the platform retro board (Jira/Confluence cross-link)

Roadmap (next 3 quarters)

Q1 (current) — Stabilization and observability
- Complete SLO rollouts for runtime-gateway and request-router.
- Migrate all production dashboards to new templated panels with SLO widgets.
- Improve autoscaler visibility: cost & cooling metrics.

Q2 — Efficiency and cost controls
- Implement token-level cost attribution for major models (first pass).
- Launch dynamic batching experiments and dashboards to measure unit cost impact.
- Expand cache telemetry (per-model KV hit-rate panels).

Q3 — Resilience and private deployments support
- Add multi-region failover playbooks and automated traffic-routing demos.
- Harden on-prem monitoring stack and runbooks for Private deployments.

Roadmap governance

- Roadmap items that affect SLOs or oncall workload require a pre-launch runbook review and a post-launch health check at 72 hours.
- All changes to alert thresholds or SLO definitions must be reviewed by the Platform SLO council (monthly).

Team wiki organization and living documents

Canonical folders (confluence pages) under eng-platform/wiki:
- /inventory — service cards (owner, SLOs, links)
- /runbooks — active runbooks per service (required template)
- /dashboards — dashboard links and panel ownership
- /retros — recent postmortems and action item tracker
- /howtos — onboarding, dashboard creation, alert tuning, and Grafana/Prometheus examples

Howtos (short checklist examples)
- Creating a new dashboard:
  1. Fork the dashboard template from /dashboards/template.
  2. Add SLO widgets (error budget and latency percentiles).
  3. Add owner and review tag, then request review from oncall lead.
  4. Deploy to Grafana using `platform-dashboard-ci` with the dashboard JSON.
- Tuning an alert:
  1. Confirm that the alert targets an SLI (error-rate, latency quantile) rather than raw internal metric.
  2. Simulate load in staging (k6) and measure false-positive rate.
  3. Update threshold and add a runbook note with reasoning.

Operational run cadence

- Weekly operations review (30m) — open action items, rising alerts, and deploy risk review.
- Quarterly SLO review (60m) — cross-team review of SLOs, burn-rate, and roadmap impacts.
- Monthly runbook audit — ensure all production runbooks updated in last 90 days.

Change and release practices affecting platform health

- All changes that modify request routing, autoscaler, or cache behavior require:
  1) Runbook review by platform-oncall (pre-flag)
  2) Canary traffic test (10% for 30 minutes)
  3) Health check and rollback window defined before full rollout

Appendices and useful queries
- Example PromQL for p99 latency: `histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le))`
- Error budget calculation snippet: `1 - (good_requests / total_requests)` where good_requests = success responses under SLO threshold.

Related pages and references
- Platform SLO policy — /confluence/eng-sre/slo-policy
- Grafana dashboard template — /confluence/eng-platform/dashboards/template
- Incident playbooks — /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/index

Next steps and action items
- All service owners: verify runbook presence and dashboard ownership within 14 days.
- Oncall leads (Elena Kim, Jordan Lee): schedule runbook audit for March 2026.

If you have suggested edits or gaps to this document, open a PR on the team wiki or ping the platform-oncall Slack channel.
